entities.name: PMID:25440352
observations: In a consecutive Irish Stroke/TIA Register cohort (n=185; 130 ischemic strokes), abnormal admission troponin-I was associated with delayed AF detected after a sinus-rhythm admission ECG; delayed AF occurred in 30% with abnormal TnI versus 6.1% with normal TnI. Abnormal TnI independently predicted delayed AF in multivariable regression (OR 5.8, P=.037); only 10 delayed-AF events were detected on telemetry, and the assay cutoff was unspecified in the abstract.

entities.name: PMID:41226937
observations: In a retrospective ischemic-stroke registry, admission hs-cTnI at or above the 99th percentile independently predicted AF detected after stroke; 121 of 1,019 analyzed patients developed AFDAS during median 22.5-month follow-up. The abstract did not report the adjusted effect estimate or confidence interval.

entities.name: PMID:37021168
observations: A 2023 systematic review of 21 studies and 4,640 patients found cardiac biomarkers had modest-to-good discrimination for newly detected AF, but troponin-I/T were evaluated in only four studies, reporting was inconsistent, overall risk of bias was high, and only BNP had external validation.

entities.name: PMID:39470526
observations: A prospective ischemic-stroke case-control study (n=117) found admission hs-cTnI significantly associated with AF status after prolonged Holter monitoring, but did not report a troponin-specific cutoff, effect estimate, or confidence interval; NT-proBNP had the strongest reported discrimination.
